ei.title: Agriculture and the Rise of Specialization
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council. The development of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10 kg of grain from each 1 kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses. With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups grew in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.

✅ ① How Farming Surpluses Built Specialized Societies (농업 잉여가 어떻게 전문화된 사회를 만들었는가): 식량 잉여 → 비농민·전문가 → 도시화·전문화·안정이라는 핵심 ← 정답
❌ ② The Lost Skills of Hunter-Gatherer Tribes (수렵 채집 부족의 사라진 기술): 수렵 채집은 도입부일 뿐
❌ ③ Why Village Councils Always Fail to Lead (마을 의회가 항상 지도에 실패하는 이유): 본문과 무관
❌ ④ The Dangers of Growing Too Much Food (식량 과잉 생산의 위험): 잉여를 긍정적으로 봄, 반대

questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council. The development of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10 kg of grain from each 1 kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. <u>In return</u>, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses. With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups grew in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>In return</u>이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: In return = 농민의 식량 지원에 대한 보답으로
det.analysis:
밑줄: 'Part of this surplus ... provided support for nonfarmers .... <u>In return</u>, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security' — 농민의 식량 지원에 대한 '보답으로'

❌ ① 대가 없이 기부: 서로 주고받는 관계이므로 틀림
❌ ② 비농민이 농사일 대신: 비농민은 농사를 짓지 않음
✅ ③ 농민의 식량 지원에 대한 보답으로 비농민이 역할을 제공: 식량(농민) ↔ 지도력·안보(비농민)의 상호 교환 ← 정답
❌ ④ 경쟁 관계: 상호 지원 관계이므로 틀림
det.tip: In return = 그 보답으로 (상호 교환 관계)

ch: 농민들이 아무런 대가 없이 식량을 기부했다는 뜻이다
농민의 식량 지원에 대한 보답으로 비농민이 역할을 제공했다는 뜻이다
농민과 비농민이 서로 경쟁 관계였다는 뜻이다
